title: Detached HEAD and the wrong branch
summary: What detached HEAD really means, how to keep work made there, and the two-command fix for commits made on the wrong branch.

steps.title: Detached HEAD
body: Normally HEAD names a branch. If you switch to a **commit** (or a tag, or `origin/main`) instead, HEAD holds that commit's id directly: **detached HEAD**.
```text
git switch --detach v1.4.0       # or: git checkout a1b2c3d
A---B---C---D   main
HEAD (detached)
It is not an error. It is perfect for looking around, building an old version, or running a quick experiment. But commits made here belong to **no branch**:
```text
A---B---C---D   main
X---Y   HEAD (detached)      <- switch away and nothing names X or Y
If you want to keep them, give them a name before (or soon after) leaving:
```text
git switch -c experiment     # while still detached: a branch at Y
git branch experiment Y      # after leaving: Y is in the reflog / the warning message

steps.prompt: You ran `git switch --detach a1b2c3d`, made two commits, and then `git switch main`. Git printed a warning about *leaving 2 commits behind*. Are they lost?
options: No: they still exist; the warning (and `git reflog`) shows the id, and `git branch keep <id>` saves them
Yes: detached commits are deleted on switch
Yes, unless you had pushed them
No: they were automatically added to main
steps.explain: Nothing is deleted until garbage collection, weeks later. Name the commit and it is an ordinary branch.

steps.prompt: Starting with `main` at C, you run the commands below. What does `git branch --contains Y` print? (Write nothing but the output; if no branch contains Y, write `(none)`.)
steps.explain: X and Y were made on a detached HEAD, so no branch points at them or their descendants. They are reachable only from the reflog until you name them.
hints: Which branch moved when you committed?
With HEAD detached, committing moves only HEAD itself.

steps.title: Committed to the wrong branch
body: You meant to start a branch, but made 3 commits directly on `main` (not pushed yet).
**To a new branch** (the commits should not be on main at all):
```text
git branch feature/coupons     # a new pointer at the current commit: it has all 3
git reset --hard HEAD~3        # move main back where it was
git switch feature/coupons
**To an existing branch**:
```text
git switch feature/coupons
git cherry-pick main~3..main   # copy the 3 commits
git switch main
git reset --hard HEAD~3        # remove them from main
Already pushed to `main`? Then do not reset: revert them on `main` and cherry-pick onto the right branch.

steps.prompt: You made 2 commits on `main` that belong on a new branch `fix/login`. Nothing is pushed. Arrange the fix.
steps.explain: The new branch must be created **before** the reset, while main still points at the commits. Then move main back and switch to the branch.

steps.prompt: Why does `git branch feature` + `git reset --hard HEAD~3` not lose the commits, even though `--hard` is involved?
options: `feature` still points at the newest of the three commits, so they stay reachable; and the working tree had no uncommitted changes to lose
Because the commits are pushed automatically
It does lose them; they must be recovered from the reflog
steps.explain: A branch is a pointer. Create it first and the commits have a name. Always check `git status` is clean before any `--hard`.

items: In the middle of a rebase
steps.explain: Rebase and bisect detach HEAD while they work, then reattach at the end. That is why `git status` says *HEAD detached at ...* in the middle of a rebase.

steps.prompt: Match the situation to the fix.
pairs: Made commits while detached; still there
Made commits while detached; already left
3 unpushed commits on main belong on a new branch
Pushed a commit to the wrong branch
revert it there, cherry-pick it to the right one

steps.prompt: Complete the commands to copy the last 2 commits of `main` onto the existing branch `feature`.
steps.explain: `main~2..main` means *commits reachable from main but not from main~2*: exactly the last two. `--hard` then removes them from main (they now live on feature).

steps.title: Simulate refs and HEAD
prompt: Build a tiny model of refs to check your understanding. Write `Simulate(List<string> commands)`.
Start with branch `main` pointing at nothing (`null`) and HEAD attached to `main`. Commands:
| `commit X` | new commit `X` whose parent is the current commit; moves the attached branch, or HEAD itself if detached |
| `branch N` | branch `N` at the current commit (HEAD does not move) |
| `reset --hard HEAD~n` | move the attached branch (or detached HEAD) back `n` parents |
Return `"HEAD -> <branch>"` or `"HEAD detached at <id>"`, then `"; "`, then every branch as `name=id` sorted by name, separated by spaces.
commit A, commit B, branch fix, reset --hard HEAD~1   ->   "HEAD -> main; fix=B main=A"
solution: var branches = new Dictionary<string, string?> { ["main"] = null };
string? Current() => attached is null ? detachedAt : branches[attached];
if (attached is null) detachedAt = p[1]; else branches[attached] = p[1];
for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) c = parent[c!];
if (attached is null) detachedAt = c; else branches[attached] = c;
var head = attached is null ? $"HEAD detached at {detachedAt}" : $"HEAD -> {attached}";
hints: Keep `Dictionary<string, string?> branches`, a `parent` dictionary, `attached` (branch name or null) and `detachedAt`.
A local function `Current()` returns the commit HEAD resolves to.
For `reset`, parse `n` from `p[2].Split('~')[1]` and walk `parent` n times.
template: Dojo.Eq("example", "HEAD -> main; fix=B main=A", Simulate(new() { "commit A", "commit B", "branch fix", "reset --hard HEAD~1" }));
Dojo.Eq("detached commits are on no branch", "HEAD -> main; main=B",
Simulate(new() { "commit A", "commit B", "switch --detach A", "commit X", "commit Y", "switch main" }));
Dojo.Eq("still detached", "HEAD detached at Y; main=B",
Simulate(new() { "commit A", "commit B", "switch --detach A", "commit X", "commit Y" }));
Dojo.Eq("rescue: name it before leaving", "HEAD -> main; keep=Y main=B",
Simulate(new() { "commit A", "commit B", "switch --detach A", "commit X", "commit Y", "branch keep", "switch main" }));
Dojo.Eq("committed on the wrong branch, fixed", "HEAD -> feature; feature=D main=B",
Simulate(new() { "commit A", "commit B", "commit C", "commit D", "branch feature", "reset --hard HEAD~2", "switch feature" }));
